# StatedFlow { #timetoalign.timelines.StatedFlow }

```python
timelines.StatedFlow()
```

What writing the order of measures a source states wrote.

## Attributes {.doc-section .doc-section-attributes}

| Name       | Type                                                                      | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
|------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| regions    | [tuple](`tuple`)\[[Region](`timetoalign.timelines.regions.Region`), ...\] | The stretches of consecutive measures the order plays, Regions of the timeline in the order first played; a stretch played more than once is one Region.                                                                         |
| flow_map   | [FlowMap](`timetoalign.timelines.flow.flowmap.FlowMap`)                   | The FlowMap listing those Regions in the order stated. It follows no convention and its provenance gives the method ``imported``.                                                                                                |
| differs_at | [Coordinate](`timetoalign.core.Coordinate`) \| None                       | Where the default flow of the timeline's flow control first plays something else than the stated order: the position along the played flow up to which the two agree, on the timeline's unit. None where they are the same flow. |
